text: If you make a prediction, you can compare it to the answer to get an error.
If you turn that error into a number for how bad the prediction was, you get a loss.
If you ask which direction would make that loss smaller, you get a gradient.
If you take a small step downhill, you get a gradient descent step.
If you repeat that step over and over, you get training.
If you do that across millions of examples, you get a trained model.
If that model learns patterns from data and uses them to make predictions, you get machine learning.
If you scale that up with huge data sets, huge models, and huge amounts of compute, you get modern AI.
And if you rewind all of it, you get one prediction.
